record.original_question: Given a projective variety X with mild singularities and a maximal rationally connected (MRC) fibration phi: X -> Y defined only up to birational modification of the base, under what assumptions can one choose a birational model of Y so that the MRC fibration is represented by a holomorphic morphism rather than merely an almost holomorphic rational map?

evidence.quote: The author does not know an example of smooth projective varieties (or varieties with mild singularities) admitting no holomorphic MRC fibration.
Problem 2.1. When do we choose an MRC fibration to be holomorphic from the ambiguities in the choices of Y ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a projective variety with at worst mild singularities (e.g., smooth, or with terminal/canonical singularities). A maximal rationally connected (MRC) fibration of $X$ is a dominant rational map $\varphi : X \dashrightarrow Y$, defined up to birational equivalence of the base $Y$, whose general fibers are rationally connected and which is maximal with this property; equivalently, every rationally connected subvariety through a very general point of $X$ is contracted by $\varphi$. By a theorem of Kollár–Miyaoka–Mori (and Graber–Harris–Starr), $\varphi$ exists and can be chosen to be an almost holomorphic rational map (i.e., its general fiber is contained in the locus where $\varphi$ is defined), with $Y$ non-uniruled.

Determine general structural conditions on $X$ (and on the choice of a birational model of $Y$) under which the MRC fibration can be represented by an actual holomorphic morphism $\varphi : X \to Y'$ to some projective variety $Y'$ birational to $Y$, rather than merely by an almost holomorphic rational map. In particular, decide whether there exists a smooth (or mildly singular) projective variety $X$ admitting no holomorphic representative of its MRC fibration for any birational choice of the base.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of when an MRC fibration can be chosen holomorphic (and whether a smooth projective variety exists admitting no holomorphic MRC fibration) appears open in general. Partial positive results exist for special classes, e.g., smooth projective varieties with pseudo-effective tangent bundle admit holomorphic MRC fibrations to smooth projective bases, but no general criterion or counterexample is known.

status_evidence.title: Families of rationally connected varieties (Graber–Harris–Starr)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes existence of MRC fibration as an almost holomorphic rational map with rationally connected general fibers and non-uniruled base.
status_evidence.claim: MRC fibration exists as almost holomorphic map; holomorphicity not asserted in general.

status_evidence.title: Minimal Models for Highly Connected Varieties
status_evidence.snippet: For varieties with pseudo-effective tangent bundle, there exists a holomorphic MRC fibration to a smooth projective variety.
status_evidence.claim: Holomorphic MRC fibrations are known under special positivity assumptions, supporting that the general case remains open.
